clue.text: Rats! One's spurned for love, close to distraught state

indicators.note: the one is rejected and something else is taken in its place, so this swaps one letter for another

parts.note: rats are pests, collectively vermin
one is the Roman numeral I
love is nil in tennis, so the letter O

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, so take the last of distraught

explanation.surface: Someone cursing as a romance falls apart, leaving them nearly distraught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats!' looks like an exclamation but is the noun: VERMIN, with its I (one) swapped for O (love) by 'spurned for', gives VERMON; 'close to' adds the T ending distraught.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in New England, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Roman sex guru's a mug

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which in Roman numerals is VI
a guru is a wise teacher, a sage

explanation.surface: A Roman sex expert is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals; 'mug' is slang for the face, not a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is slang for the face, and the answer is a literary word for the face.

clue.text: Search for food, turning to large caviar sandwiches

indicators.note: caviar here encloses the other letters like bread round a filling

parts.note: caviar is fish roe

indicators.note: turning the little word round makes it read backwards

explanation.surface: A forager moving on to big caviar sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes OT of 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage, as a pig does when it turns up the soil with its snout looking for something to eat.

clue.text: Quaint style's back after odd Orwell novel

indicators.note: after puts the end of style behind the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters are made into something fresh
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A bookish verdict: a strange Orwell novel marks a return to quaintness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but here it is the anagram signal; 'after' sets the last letter of 'style' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-antique phrase for a self-consciously old-fashioned, twee look, the sort of thing called quaint.

clue.text: Movement that's in time runs to a climax

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a climax is the culmination, the end

explanation.surface: A musical or political movement that is in fashion builds to its peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A general direction or drift of change, as a tendency is a movement of opinion or prices.

clue.text: Conservative certainly not about to be socially aware

parts.note: the Conservatives are the party of the political right

indicators.note: about signals turning the refusal round to read the other way

parts.note: an emphatic refusal is no

explanation.surface: A Tory who is certainly not about to become progressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks as if it means 'on the point of', but here it turns the refusal round.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial idiom for someone holding fashionably progressive, liberal views.

clue.text: Back what the children's guardian must do

definitions.meaning: towards the rear, as an adverb

definitions.text: what the children's guardian must do
definitions.meaning: a guardian must bring up the children in their care: raise the young ones placed under protection

explanation.surface: The legal duties of someone left looking after a family's children.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it 4,5: to rear (bring up) wards (children under a guardian).
explanation.definitionFit: Directed towards the back or behind, a synonym for backwards.

clue.text: Carriage door's sound

indicators.note: sound signals a word that is the same when spoken as another

parts.note: a gate is a door in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A coach door making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' looks like a coach; here it is posture, how one carries oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way a person holds and moves their body, as is the manner of walking.

clue.text: Time, an hour after midnight, to get music and liqueur

parts.note: one o'clock in the morning, I (Roman one) plus AM
an aria is a piece of solo vocal music

explanation.surface: Late-night revelry: at one in the morning it's music and a nightcap.
explanation.walkthrough: 1am written with the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican coffee-flavoured brand of liqueur, an example of the drink.

clue.text: Annoying lover of Heather may well!

definitions.meaning: irritating with repeated digs, a present participle
heather is ling, so one fond of the plant may well require some: split 4,4

explanation.surface: Someone moaning about a pestering admirer of a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant ling; the answer split 4,4 says what her lover would do.
explanation.definitionFit: Provoking with constant small jibes, as a synonym for irritating or goading.

clue.text: 24 down is found at the end of this puzzle

indicators.note: only the closing stretch of the word for this puzzle is kept, its opening four letters dropped

parts.note: the thing being solved is a cross-word puzzle

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying the other answer turns up at the bottom of the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is EPEE, the fencing weapon; the closing five letters of the word for this puzzle give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An epee is a kind of fencing blade, so the answer is the general weapon it exemplifies.

clue.text: Ecstasy and speed? Swallowing flipping LSD, get weed out

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: the outer letters take the reversed drug inside them like a mouthful

parts.note: speed is a rate

indicators.note: flipping turns the drug's name over so it reads backwards

parts.note: LSD is the drug acid

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled night, with someone told to get the cannabis out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns the drug round and 'Swallowing' puts it inside. 'Ecstasy', 'speed' and 'weed' all look like drugs; only the first is one here.

clue.text: Desperate housewives go wild, so excited about fellow's clothing

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the piece from fellow
excited letters are stirred up into a new order
the clothing of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: GOWILDSO is shuffled ('excited') to GOLIDOWS around FW, the outside of 'fellow' ('clothing').
explanation.definitionFit: Wives left alone while husbands spend all day on the links, wittily cast as the TV drama's desperate women.

clue.text: Old lady's going to walk

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, MA, and the 's is 'is', which with going to makes the contraction
'll is the contraction of will, meaning is going to

explanation.surface: Mum announces she is heading out on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as MA'LL, 'Ma will', which is what 'Old lady's going to' means.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree-lined promenade, as London's famous Pall Mall-style public walk, a noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Most uncommon to cover news in tropical region

indicators.note: the outer word covers the other by wrapping around it

parts.note: most uncommon is rarest
news is info, information

explanation.surface: A very rare chance to report the news from the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense evergreen jungle with heavy rainfall, found mostly near the equator, as in the Amazon.

clue.text: Improvement in how sappers are deployed?

parts.note: sappers are the Royal Engineers, RE
how troops are deployed is their formation, the arrangement they take up

explanation.surface: A question whether redeploying army engineers would make things better.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'how ... are deployed' wraps around 'sappers': RE in formation.
explanation.definitionFit: Reform is improvement by correcting faults, the noun used for moral or institutional betterment.

clue.text: "The commonness of the fellow! Rule by the Prince of Wales's no good", the Queen admitted

indicators.note: the shortened period lets the monarch's letters in, enclosing them
no says the letter is not wanted, so it is taken out

parts.words: Rule by the Prince of Wales's
parts.note: the Prince of Wales ruled for George III from 1811 to 1820, the Regency

explanation.surface: An aristocratic outburst at a fellow's vulgarity, with grumbles about royal rule.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Wales ruled as Prince Regent for George III from 1811 to 1820; 'no' removes the G and 'admitted' lets the Queen in.
explanation.definitionFit: How often something occurs; commonness is how common a thing is, a near synonym of the rate.

clue.text: Delayed returning to wrap present that's heavenly

indicators.note: the reversed word wraps round the other like paper round a gift
returning sends the word for delayed back the other way

parts.note: delayed means late
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A late gift, still wrapped, that is divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes ETAL of LATE; 'present' looks like a gift but means HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicately light and other-worldly, as of the celestial sphere, a synonym of heavenly.

clue.text: Stew for American frontiersmen?

parts.note: read the answer's second word as an anagram, signalled by its first word, and it makes the clue's word

explanation.surface: A cowboy cookpot dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, is 'wild' (rearranged) + the four letters of a direction, which give the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawless frontier region of the nineteenth-century US, home of cowboys and pioneers, so loosely their land.

clue.text: Pervert tries high definition porn, but not you or I!

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist out of shape, so the letters are distorted

explanation.surface: Someone pervy tries HD porn, but the speaker insists it was neither of us.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIES + HD + PORN, rearranged by 'Pervert'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'you' is second person and 'I' first, so what is neither is the remaining category: he, she, it, they.

clue.text: English runner always going in opposing directions

indicators.note: going in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: south and north are opposite compass points
always means ever

explanation.surface: An English athlete forever heading off in different directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river here, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's longest river, rising in Wales and flowing through England, a runner in the sense of flowing water.

clue.text: Horse put in pen to struggle

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to pen something is to write it
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A horse being led into a pen, fighting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' and 'pen' look like animal and enclosure; they are heroin (H) and the verb to write.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist and squirm in pain or effort, a synonym of struggle.

clue.text: Nerdy, dry, oddly repressed Christian Scientist

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are held down, so only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A dull, dry, buttoned-up religious type.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Baker Eddy founded the Christian Science movement in 1879, so she is its best-known adherent.

clue.text: He gets rid of lots of gold, tossing in ore etc

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: tossing throws the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: A miner disposing of a lot of gold by throwing it in with ore and the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of gold' looks like one phrase; the definition ends at 'lots', and 'of' joins. INOREETC rearranged by 'tossing' gives CTIONEER.

clue.text: Picked up wrong cake

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.definitionFit: A rich layered gateau of central European origin, an example of a cake.

clue.text: Goalie stripped off and raised arm

stripping off removes the outside letters of the word

parts.note: a goalie is a goalkeeper, keeper

explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped off' leaves EEPE of KEEPER; 'raised' turns it upwards in this down light.

clue.text: Getting boundaries in early, English batsman's a revelation

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: Something surprising that suddenly shows the truth, an idiomatic synonym for revelation.

explanation.walkthrough: 'kicking' drops R from the front ('at first') of the six-letter word for return.
explanation.definitionFit: Chris Evert was a leading American women's champion of the 1970s and 1980s.

clue.text: Take a punt on this lake, with yen to catch aquatic creature

indicators.note: the outer letters surround and hold the creature

explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' looks like a flat boat on the lake; here it is a gamble.

clue.text: Understanding 10 x 3 only partially

parts.note: ten three times over, written out as words
